q: For any trapped sample of gas, we can measure its temperature, volume, pressure, and _____.
e: The four measurable quantities are temperature, volume, pressure, and mass.

q: The units of temperature are degree Celsius, degree Fahrenheit, and _____.
e: The three units of temperature mentioned are Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin.

q: The relationship between Celsius and Kelvin is expressed as $T^{\circ}\text{C} + 273 = $ _____.
e: The formula to convert Celsius to Kelvin is $T^{\circ}\text{C} + 273 = T\text{K}$.

q: The boiling point of water is $100^{\circ}\text{C}$, which is equal to _____ on the Kelvin scale.
Normal human body temperature is $37^{\circ}\text{C}$, which is equal to _____ on the Kelvin scale.
Absolute zero is _____ on the Celsius scale.
e: Absolute zero is defined as $-273^{\circ}\text{C}$ (or more precisely $-273.15^{\circ}\text{C}$).

q: Absolute zero is _____ on the Kelvin scale.
e: Absolute zero is the zero point of the Kelvin scale, $0\text{K}$.

q: The relation between volume units is $1000\text{ cm}^3 = 1000\text{ mL} = 1\text{ L} = $ _____.
e: 1 Liter is exactly equal to $1\text{ dm}^3$ and $1000\text{ cm}^3$.

q: Pressure is the _____ that acts on a given area.
e: Pressure is defined as the force that acts on a given area.

q: The SI unit of pressure is the _____, which is equal to $1\text{ N m}^{-2}$.
e: The pascal (Pa) is the SI unit of pressure, equal to $1\text{ N m}^{-2}$.

q: The mixture of gases surrounding the Earth is known as our _____.
e: The mixture of gases surrounding the Earth is called the atmosphere.

q: Atmospheric pressure is the force exerted on a surface by the air above it as _____ pulls it to the Earth.
e: Gravity pulls the air down, exerting atmospheric pressure on surfaces.

q: The instrument used for measuring atmospheric pressure is a _____.
e: A barometer is the instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure.

q: The instrument used for measuring gas pressure is a _____.
e: A manometer is the instrument used to measure gas pressure.

q: Standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm) supports a column of mercury exactly _____ high at $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ at sea level.
e: Standard atmospheric pressure supports a $760\text{ mm}$ column of mercury.

q: The mmHg unit is also the same as the _____.
e: The text states that the mmHg unit is the same as the torr.
$1\text{ atm}$ is exactly equal to $101,325\text{ Pa}$.

q: The mass of a gas can be determined by weighing the gas in an enclosed container by gram (g) or _____.
e: Gas mass is determined in grams (g) or kilograms (kg).
